assertion.prompt: Which Long COVID mechanisms are persistent upstream drivers versus self-sustaining downstream consequences after SARS-CoV-2 viral clearance?
assertion.rationale: The current graph places SARS-CoV-2 persistence upstream of immune activation, serotonin depletion, mast-cell activation, and other downstream nodes, but established Long COVID may include virus-independent immune, endothelial, autonomic, or autoimmune loops. The PAX LC nirmatrelvir-ritonavir trial did not significantly improve health outcomes at day 28, which does not refute viral persistence but makes the active-replicating-virus model insufficient as a single explanation for established disease. Resolving this hierarchy requires separating replication-competent virus, residual antigen/RNA, and self-sustaining downstream pathology in the same patients over time.

proposed_experiments.name: Viral-RNA-positive versus viral-RNA-negative Long COVID single-cell profiling
proposed_experiments.description: Enroll Long COVID patients stratified by tissue or blood evidence of SARS-CoV-2 RNA/antigen, then compare single-cell immune states, endothelial activation markers, autoantibodies, serotonin/tryptophan metabolites, and autonomic testing against matched viral-marker-negative Long COVID and recovered-control groups.
proposed_experiments.decision_criterion: Viral-positive patients show a distinct upstream antigen-response program that temporally precedes downstream immune, vascular, metabolic, or autonomic abnormalities; viral-negative patients retain downstream abnormalities only if these programs are self-sustaining.

proposed_experiments.name: Viral-reservoir-stratified antiviral trial with downstream biomarker endpoints
proposed_experiments.description: Randomize only patients with pre-specified SARS-CoV-2 persistence biomarkers to antiviral or placebo arms, and measure viral markers alongside immune activation, microvascular, autonomic, and symptom endpoints to test whether viral clearance is necessary and sufficient for downstream disease reversal.
proposed_experiments.decision_criterion: Antiviral-mediated reduction of viral biomarkers must precede and predict improvement in downstream immune/microvascular/autonomic endpoints; viral clearance without downstream improvement would support self-sustaining post-viral pathology.

assertion.prompt: What are the true frequencies of each phenotype in AGTPBP1-related disease?
assertion.rationale: The available denominators are small, retrospective literature-series samples with variable severity and per-feature assessment. The review reports muscle atrophy in half of patients and reflex alterations in almost all, but the latter combines opposite reflex directions and the former does not require neurogenic verification. Neither aggregate is assigned to a narrower phenotype. Prospective consistently ascertained denominators are lacking.

proposed_experiments.name: Registry-based phenotype frequency estimation
proposed_experiments.description: Collect uniformly phenotyped, consecutively ascertained AGTPBP1 cases so that per-phenotype frequencies have a common denominator rather than being pooled across severity-ascertained case reports.

selected_evidence.snippet: Alterations in tendon reflexes were observed in almost all individuals.

assertion.prompt: Which unusual findings recur in genetically secure cases?
assertion.rationale: The 2024 likely-pathogenic p.Thr884Pro patient had coarse facies, narrow forehead, thick eyebrows, broad bulbous nose, short philtrum, thick lips and large ears; arachnodactyly, interphalangeal hyperextensibility, low-inserted thumbs, toe camptodactyly, prominent heels, scoliosis and joint contractures were also described. Table 2 additionally records brisk reflexes, hypometric saccades and poor eye contact, and ERG showed retinal dysfunction. The extensor plantar response in the 4.5-month-old autopsy case is not separately treated as a pathological Babinski sign because that response can be physiological at this age. These are preserved as a case expansion whose individual causal attribution and recurrence are unresolved. The second AGTPBP1 patient carried p.Thr512Ala classified as a VUS and had strabismus, oculomotor apraxia, optic-nerve dysfunction and contractures; that case is not pooled as equally established genetic evidence. Mouse retinal degeneration is not substituted for these human observations.

selected_evidence.snippet: He had multiple skeletal deformities “arachnodactyly, bilateral hyperextensibility of the interphalangeal joints, bilateral low inserted thumb, toes camptodactyly, bilateral prominent heel, severe scoliosis and joint contractures” and bilateral fungal infection of both feet (Fig. 3).

assertion.prompt: Which neural regions account for the remaining movement, ocular and sensory manifestations?
assertion.rationale: Spasticity indicates a central motor component, but the reviewed human studies do not establish the affected descending pathways. Dystonia and seizures coexist with caudate/putaminal atrophy in one case without demonstrating that this lesion causes either symptom. Hand tremor includes rest and action components, and the sporadic hearing loss is unlocalized. The broad eye-movement relation to weakness/cerebellar dysfunction is represented, while the specific origins of apraxia and esotropia are not separated. Microcephaly includes postnatal head-growth decline, but neither cerebellar loss nor peripheral motor-neuron loss alone has been shown to explain it; the first 2019 case also had a potentially contributing NCAPD3 variant. These gaps concern lesion or causal attribution, not simply absent pathway nodes.

assertion.prompt: Are activated lymph node stromal cells the source that drives the Castleman cytokine excess, or do they expand and secrete in response to a cytokine excess generated elsewhere?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#Lymph Node Stromal Cell Activation and Expansion
assertion.rationale: The spatial data establish where VEGF and IL-6 transcripts are, not what started them. The question is not academic: if stromal cells are the driver, stroma-directed agents (lymphotoxin-beta receptor fusion proteins, VEGF inhibitors, NOTCH inhibitors) are rational; if they are responders, those agents treat a consequence. The evidence is one observational cohort of 22 cases with no perturbation, and the subtype-specific IL-6 source data point the other way for TAFRO, where endothelial IL-6 is proposed to be secondary to the cytokine storm.

assertion.prompt: What initiates idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease - autoimmunity, an ectopic clonal cytokine source, a non-HHV-8 infection, or a germline inflammatory predisposition?
assertion.rationale: This is the field's central unanswered question and everything downstream depends on it. Three candidate processes were formally proposed in 2014 and none has been confirmed or excluded since. Viral-Track sequencing of 22 UCD and 19 iMCD nodes found no shared viral signature, weakening the infectious candidate; autoantibody enrichment supports but does not establish the autoimmune candidate; and recurrent somatic alleles support but do not establish a clonal candidate. Because the etiology is unknown, iMCD is defined by exclusion, has no diagnostic biomarker, and is treated with a single-cytokine blockade that fails in most patients.

proposed_experiments.name: Paired serologic, viral, and clonality screen across adjudicated iMCD subtypes
proposed_experiments.description: In a prospectively enrolled, expert-adjudicated iMCD cohort stratified by TAFRO/IPL/NOS, run in parallel on the same patients: unbiased autoantigen-array and functional receptor-blocking serology, metagenomic and viral-capture sequencing of lymph node and plasma, and deep targeted sequencing of sorted stromal, plasma cell, and T cell fractions for clonality. Testing the three candidate etiologies on shared samples is what makes them comparable; the existing evidence for each comes from separate cohorts.
supporting_outcome: A candidate process is enriched in one subtype and co-segregates with disease activity, with the other two candidates negative in the same patients.
refuting_outcome: All three candidate processes are negative or are equally present in disease controls, indicating the initiating process lies outside the three proposed categories.

selected_evidence.snippet: While uncontrolled infection with human herpesvirus-8 (HHV-8) is responsible for the cytokine storm in a portion of multicentric CD (HHV-8-associated MCD) cases, the etiology of unicentric CD (UCD) and HHV-8-negative/idiopathic MCD (iMCD) is unknown.

assertion.prompt: Which mediator causes the glomerular endothelial injury of TAFRO, and would targeting it prevent the dialysis requirement?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#Endothelial Injury and Renal Thrombotic Microangiopathy
assertion.rationale: Renal failure is the most common post-diagnosis morbidity in iMCD (48%) and 27% of patients require dialysis, so the renal lesion drives a large share of the disease's burden. The histology - membranoproliferative-like injury and thrombotic microangiopathy - points at glomerular endothelium, and IL-6 and VEGF are the proposed mediators, but the review that summarizes this states plainly that their role in renal injury is not well understood. No therapy is directed at the renal lesion specifically.

proposed_experiments.name: Spatial mediator mapping of TAFRO renal biopsies
proposed_experiments.description: Apply the same spatial transcriptomic and in situ hybridization panel used on Castleman lymph nodes to banked TAFRO kidney biopsies, localizing IL6, VEGFA, complement components, and endothelial injury markers to glomerular compartments, and compare with thrombotic microangiopathy from other causes and with membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis controls.
would_support: pathophysiology#Endothelial Injury and Renal Thrombotic Microangiopathy
supporting_outcome: A specific mediator localizes to injured glomerular endothelium in TAFRO but not in the comparator lesions, nominating a renal-directed target.
refuting_outcome: The TAFRO renal lesion is indistinguishable from other causes of thrombotic microangiopathy, indicating a shared final common pathway rather than a Castleman-specific mediator.

assertion.prompt: Does iMCD raise the risk of subsequent myeloid and solid malignancy, or is the reported excess an artifact of misclassifying malignancy-associated reactive lymphadenopathy as iMCD?

The two readings have opposite implications: an excess means iMCD warrants cancer surveillance, whereas an artifact means claims-based iMCD cohorts contain patients who only ever had a malignancy. There is no known diagnostic serum biomarker, which the natural history study names as a contributor to underdiagnosis. CXCL13 is the closest candidate but was validated as a predictor of siltuximab response, not as a diagnostic discriminator, and the reported comparison groups included related diseases rather than the full mimic set a diagnostic test would face.

supporting_outcome: A marker or panel separates iMCD from every individual mimic at clinically useful sensitivity and specificity.
refuting_outcome: Candidate markers separate iMCD from healthy controls but not from individual mimics, confirming that diagnosis by exclusion is unavoidable with serum markers alone.

assertion.prompt: What drives disease in the majority of iMCD patients who do not respond to IL-6 blockade, and can non-responders be identified before weeks of failed therapy have passed?

What drives the remaining non-responders is not known.

refuting_outcome: Response rates are the same regardless of pretreatment endotype, indicating the proposed endotypes are descriptive rather than predictive.

assertion.prompt: If NS6 is caused by gain-of-function NRAS alleles that raise RAS-MAPK flux, why do 1p13.2 microdeletions that remove one NRAS copy produce an overlapping Noonan phenotype?
assertion.rationale: The canonical MAPK interpretation of NS6 involves increased signal throughput into RAF-MEK-ERK. A loss-of-dosage lesion converging on a similar clinical picture challenges a simple monotonic MAPK model; it does not establish equivalence across the parallel effector responses, including AKT. Three readings are open and the published data do not separate them: the deletion phenotype may be driven by other genes in the deleted segment rather than by NRAS; reduced N-Ras may perturb pathway output non-monotonically, so that both raising and lowering it degrades developmental signalling; or the shared features may be non-specific enough that clinical overlap does not imply mechanistic convergence. The same loss-and-gain pattern is reported for MAP2K2 and SHOC2, so this is a recurring question about RAS-MAPK dosage rather than an NRAS curiosity. Resolving it bears on whether MEK inhibition is a rational therapy for the deletion phenotype, where it could plausibly make matters worse.

proposed_experiments.name: NRAS dosage series against developmental RAS-MAPK output
proposed_experiments.description: Compare ERK pathway output and developmental phenotype across an allelic dosage series - NRAS null/heterozygous-null, wild type, and a knock-in non-hotspot NS6 allele - in one system, to test whether pathway output responds non-monotonically to N-Ras dosage or whether the deletion phenotype is carried by neighbouring genes.

readouts.name: Phosphorylated ERK as developmental RAS-MAPK output
readouts.interpretation: A similar developmental phenotype arising from opposite directions of pathway output would support non-monotonic dosage sensitivity; output changing only in the gain-of-function arm would point to neighbouring genes carrying the deletion phenotype.

assertion.prompt: Does noribogaine act as a kappa agonist or, in the elevated-dynorphin state of opioid withdrawal, as a functional antagonist, and is that difference what reconciles a kappa-agonist mechanism with an antidepressant clinical effect?
assertion.rationale: The kappa model proposes an agonist to relieve the state whose validated treatment is kappa antagonism, and ibogaine's reported antidepressant effect deepens the mismatch. The reconciliation is that noribogaine inhibits dynorphin-driven beta-arrestin recruitment more potently than it stimulates G-protein signalling, so in a high-dynorphin state it may behave as a normalizer rather than an agonist. Every measurement supporting that reading was made in heterologous systems under basal conditions, so the state-dependence the reconciliation requires has never been observed. Separately, a nonhuman-primate comparison of two biased kappa agonists attributed their milder profile to factors other than G-protein bias, which weakens the explanatory device the model leans on hardest.

proposed_experiments.name: State-dependent kappa signalling and behaviour under high dynorphin tone
proposed_experiments.description: Measure noribogaine's kappa signalling under basal and elevated dynorphin tone in the same preparation, then test whether the direction of its behavioural effect follows. In vitro, compare G-protein and beta-arrestin responses with and without a dynorphin background across the concentration range achievable in brain. In vivo, compare noribogaine's effect on intracranial self-stimulation thresholds and on conditioned place preference in opioid-naive animals against animals in spontaneous or precipitated withdrawal, where dynorphin tone is elevated.

experiment_type.preferred_term: state-dependent receptor signalling and behavioural comparison

perturbations.name: Noribogaine under basal versus elevated dynorphin tone
perturbations.description: The same compound and concentration range applied in two states, which is the comparison the normalization reading requires and that no existing study makes.

controls.name: Reference kappa agonist and reference kappa antagonist arms
controls.description: A conventional agonist and norbinaltorphimine, run in both states, to place noribogaine on a scale rather than describing it in isolation.

readouts.name: Direction of effect on reward threshold in each state
readouts.interpretation: A reversal of direction between the naive and withdrawal states is the signature of state-dependent normalization; the same direction in both states means noribogaine is simply an agonist.

proposed_experiments.decision_criterion: Direction of effect reversing between basal and high-dynorphin states supports rewriting the hypothesis as kappa-signalling normalization rather than kappa agonism. A pro-dysphoric effect in both states means the hypothesis is running in the wrong pharmacological direction and should be demoted.
supporting_outcome: Noribogaine lowers reward thresholds under elevated dynorphin tone while producing conventional kappa-agonist effects in naive animals.
refuting_outcome: Noribogaine is pro-dysphoric in both states.

assertion.prompt: Why do rodent models and uncontrolled human series report large anti-opioid effects for iboga alkaloids while the one randomized trial in opioid-dependent patients found non-significant reductions in withdrawal?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#Noradrenergic Hyperactivity and Opioid Withdrawal Syndrome
assertion.rationale: The evidence supporting every mechanism here is rodent self-administration and uncontrolled human observation, and both are prone to the same inflation. Within the preclinical corpus itself the effect is not uniform: a systematic scoping review found seven of forty studies showed no improvement over controls, three of them on ibogaine. On the human side, the randomized comparison that does exist gave noribogaine to opioid-dependent patients and produced dose-dependent QTc prolongation with withdrawal reductions that did not reach significance. The mechanistic hypotheses are being fitted to an effect whose size in controlled human testing is not established, and the strongest recent preclinical result was obtained in male rats only. This is a translational-validity gap rather than an absence of evidence, which is why it is recorded as a model mismatch.

proposed_experiments.name: Multi-site blinded replication of the iboga anti-opioid effect with both sexes
proposed_experiments.description: Run a preregistered, blinded, multi-laboratory replication of single-dose iboga alkaloid effects on opioid self-administration and reinstatement, with randomization, adequate power, both sexes, and a common protocol. Report effect sizes rather than significance, and treat the published null studies as prior observations to be reconciled rather than excluded. The purpose is to establish the size of the effect the mechanistic hypotheses are competing to explain, before further mechanism studies are designed around it.

controls.name: Blinded vehicle arm at every site
controls.description: Blinding is the specific missing control, since the reported effects come from unblinded rodent work and uncontrolled human series.

controls.name: Female cohorts at every site
controls.description: The strongest recent preclinical result was obtained in male rats only, and the metabolite's bioavailability differs by sex in rodents.

readouts.name: Effect size of the durable reduction in opioid intake
readouts.target: pathophysiology#Compulsive Opioid Seeking and Loss of Control
readouts.interpretation: A pooled effect size, with its heterogeneity across sites and sexes, replaces the current position in which single-laboratory results and published nulls sit side by side unreconciled.

proposed_experiments.decision_criterion: A replicable effect of stated size establishes the phenomenon the mechanistic hypotheses must explain and calibrates how much mechanism each needs to account for. Heterogeneity that tracks sex, strain or site relocates the question from mechanism to moderator.

assertion.prompt: Does ibogaine change GDNF or BDNF in treated patients, given that the only human neurotrophin data in opioid dependence are cross-sectional baselines in which GDNF is unchanged and BDNF, not GDNF, tracks craving?
assertion.rationale: The neurotrophic hypothesis makes a human prediction it has never been asked to meet. In opiate-dependent patients, serum BDNF is elevated and correlates with heroin craving while serum GDNF is unchanged and uncorrelated. That is a negative for the GDNF-specific claim, but not a decisive one, because a cross-sectional baseline in maintenance patients does not test what the model predicts, which is a change in GDNF following a dose. Rodent ibogaine also raises BDNF broadly across nucleus accumbens, substantia nigra and prefrontal cortex, so even a positive human neurotrophin signal would need to distinguish a GDNF-specific response from a general one.

proposed_experiments.name: Serial neurotrophin response in ibogaine-treated patients
proposed_experiments.description: In a jurisdiction where ibogaine treatment is legal, collect serial plasma and where feasible cerebrospinal fluid GDNF and BDNF from patients before dosing and at intervals through twelve weeks, alongside withdrawal, craving and abstinence measures and CYP2D6 genotype. The comparison that matters is within-subject change from each patient's own baseline, which is what the existing cross-sectional study could not provide.

readouts.name: Within-subject change in GDNF from pre-dose baseline
readouts.interpretation: The model predicts a GDNF rise after dosing; an unchanged GDNF alongside a clinical response would place the burden on a non-neurotrophic mechanism.

readouts.name: Within-subject change in BDNF from pre-dose baseline
readouts.interpretation: Measured in parallel to test whether any neurotrophin response is GDNF-specific, as the model requires, or general.

proposed_experiments.decision_criterion: A GDNF rise that precedes and predicts the clinical response, and is larger than the concurrent BDNF change, supports the neurotrophic model in humans. An unchanged GDNF with a clinical response, or a BDNF-dominant response, argues that the human mechanism is not the one the rodent ethanol experiments identified.
supporting_outcome: GDNF rises from baseline after dosing and the rise predicts abstinence.
refuting_outcome: GDNF is unchanged after dosing in patients who nonetheless respond.

assertion.prompt: Does the persistence of ibogaine's anti-opioid effect require an induced change in the brain, or can it be explained by continued drug exposure from sequestration in fat and conversion to a long-lived metabolite?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#Compulsive Opioid Seeking and Loss of Control
assertion.rationale: Every mechanism proposed for ibogaine's durability is pharmacodynamic, so the shared premise that a lasting change in the brain is required has never itself been tested. The competing explanation is on the record and was raised by the originating laboratory: both ibogaine and 18-MC are sequestered in fat, and long-term effects may reflect slow release and conversion to noribogaine rather than any induced remodelling. Human pharmacokinetics argue against this for the parent compound, whose clearance is rapid and CYP2D6-dependent, but noribogaine persists for days and no study has correlated the magnitude of the aftereffect with concurrent brain or plasma exposure. Until that is done, a positive result for any pharmacodynamic mechanism is confounded with continued occupancy of the same target.

proposed_experiments.name: Aftereffect magnitude against concurrent brain and plasma exposure
proposed_experiments.description: In rats with established opioid self-administration, give a single ibogaine dose and then sample brain, plasma and adipose ibogaine and noribogaine at intervals spanning the aftereffect, pairing every pharmacokinetic sample with a behavioural session in the same animals. Add two dissociating arms: a lipectomised or lean-versus-obese comparison that alters depot capacity without altering the administered dose, and a dosing regimen matched to reproduce the noribogaine concentration time-course without the parent compound.

experiment_type.preferred_term: paired pharmacokinetic and behavioural time-course experiment

perturbations.name: Single systemic ibogaine dose
perturbations.target: pathophysiology#Compulsive Opioid Seeking and Loss of Control
perturbations.description: The standard single-dose regimen whose aftereffect is the phenomenon in question.

perturbations.name: Depot capacity manipulation
perturbations.target: pathophysiology#Compulsive Opioid Seeking and Loss of Control
perturbations.description: Alteration of adipose depot capacity, holding administered dose constant, to change the predicted release profile without changing the pharmacodynamic exposure at dosing.

controls.name: Noribogaine-matched infusion without ibogaine
controls.description: Reproduces the metabolite exposure curve directly, separating sustained occupancy from anything the parent drug initiated.

readouts.name: Opioid intake at each time point paired with concurrent brain noribogaine
readouts.target: pathophysiology#Compulsive Opioid Seeking and Loss of Control
readouts.interpretation: The shape of the relation is the result: an aftereffect that tracks concurrent exposure is sustained occupancy, one that outlasts it is an induced change.

proposed_experiments.decision_criterion: If the aftereffect tracks concurrent brain noribogaine and scales with depot capacity, durability is pharmacokinetic and no induced-plasticity mechanism is required to explain it. If the aftereffect persists after exposure has fallen below target-engaging concentrations, a pharmacodynamic mechanism is required and the three competing hypotheses remain live.
supporting_outcome: Reduced opioid intake persisting after brain noribogaine falls below concentrations that engage any candidate target.
refuting_outcome: Aftereffect magnitude tracks concurrent exposure and scales with adipose depot capacity.

assertion.prompt: Which of the three candidate mechanisms for ibogaine's anti-opioid effect is actually necessary for it, given that no study has ever infused ibogaine itself into a candidate site, or blocked a candidate receptor, while measuring opioid self-administration?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#VTA Disinhibition and Mesolimbic Dopamine Release
pathophysiology#Compulsive Opioid Seeking and Loss of Control
assertion.rationale: Three mechanisms compete to explain the same phenotype, and each rests on a different molecule or a different reinforcer. The GDNF route has a sufficiency-and-necessity pair, but for ethanol. The habenular route has a site dissociation, but for the congener 18-MC, which does not share ibogaine's neurotrophic actions. The kappa route has sufficiency from engineered analogues, not necessity for the parent drug. Ibogaine itself has never been microinjected into any site with an opioid reinforcer, and the only reported loss-of-function test against ibogaine is a partial reversal by a kappa antagonist combined with an NMDA agonist, reported once by the originating laboratory without isolating either action. Because all three routes converge on the same behavioural endpoint, demonstrating sufficiency for any one of them cannot establish that ibogaine works through it.

proposed_experiments.name: Intracerebral ibogaine site dissociation against opioid self-administration
proposed_experiments.description: Run the He 2005 and Glick 2006 designs on the parent drug rather than on a surrogate. Rats acquiring intravenous heroin or fentanyl self-administration receive ibogaine (or noribogaine) microinjected into the ventral tegmental area, the medial habenula, or the interpeduncular nucleus, with a sucrose or food arm run in parallel to test reinforcer selectivity. Measure intake acutely and at 24 hours and one week to separate the acute effect from the aftereffect, since the aftereffect is the property all three hypotheses were built to explain.

experiment_type.preferred_term: intracerebral microinjection and operant self-administration experiment

assertion.prompt: Does noribogaine act as a kappa agonist or, in the elevated-dynorphin state of opioid withdrawal, as a functional antagonist, and is that difference what reconciles a kappa-agonist mechanism with an antidepressant clinical effect?
assertion.rationale: The kappa model proposes an agonist to relieve the state whose validated treatment is kappa antagonism, and ibogaine's reported antidepressant effect deepens the mismatch. The reconciliation is that noribogaine inhibits dynorphin-driven beta-arrestin recruitment more potently than it stimulates G-protein signalling, so in a high-dynorphin state it may behave as a normalizer rather than an agonist. Every measurement supporting that reading was made in heterologous systems under basal conditions, so the state-dependence the reconciliation requires has never been observed. Separately, a nonhuman-primate comparison of two biased kappa agonists attributed their milder profile to factors other than G-protein bias, which weakens the explanatory device the model leans on hardest.

proposed_experiments.name: State-dependent kappa signalling and behaviour under high dynorphin tone
proposed_experiments.description: Measure noribogaine's kappa signalling under basal and elevated dynorphin tone in the same preparation, then test whether the direction of its behavioural effect follows. In vitro, compare G-protein and beta-arrestin responses with and without a dynorphin background across the concentration range achievable in brain. In vivo, compare noribogaine's effect on intracranial self-stimulation thresholds and on conditioned place preference in opioid-naive animals against animals in spontaneous or precipitated withdrawal, where dynorphin tone is elevated.

experiment_type.preferred_term: state-dependent receptor signalling and behavioural comparison

perturbations.name: Noribogaine under basal versus elevated dynorphin tone
perturbations.description: The same compound and concentration range applied in two states, which is the comparison the normalization reading requires and that no existing study makes.

controls.name: Reference kappa agonist and reference kappa antagonist arms
controls.description: A conventional agonist and norbinaltorphimine, run in both states, to place noribogaine on a scale rather than describing it in isolation.

readouts.name: Direction of effect on reward threshold in each state
readouts.interpretation: A reversal of direction between the naive and withdrawal states is the signature of state-dependent normalization; the same direction in both states means noribogaine is simply an agonist.

proposed_experiments.decision_criterion: Direction of effect reversing between basal and high-dynorphin states supports rewriting the hypothesis as kappa-signalling normalization rather than kappa agonism. A pro-dysphoric effect in both states means the hypothesis is running in the wrong pharmacological direction and should be demoted.
supporting_outcome: Noribogaine lowers reward thresholds under elevated dynorphin tone while producing conventional kappa-agonist effects in naive animals.
refuting_outcome: Noribogaine is pro-dysphoric in both states.

assertion.prompt: Does the persistence of ibogaine's anti-opioid effect require an induced change in the brain, or can it be explained by continued drug exposure from sequestration in fat and conversion to a long-lived metabolite?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#Compulsive Opioid Seeking and Loss of Control
assertion.rationale: Every mechanism proposed for ibogaine's durability is pharmacodynamic, so the shared premise that a lasting change in the brain is required has never itself been tested. The competing explanation is on the record and was raised by the originating laboratory: both ibogaine and 18-MC are sequestered in fat, and long-term effects may reflect slow release and conversion to noribogaine rather than any induced remodelling. Human pharmacokinetics argue against this for the parent compound, whose clearance is rapid and CYP2D6-dependent, but noribogaine persists for days and no study has correlated the magnitude of the aftereffect with concurrent brain or plasma exposure. Until that is done, a positive result for any pharmacodynamic mechanism is confounded with continued occupancy of the same target.

proposed_experiments.name: Aftereffect magnitude against concurrent brain and plasma exposure
proposed_experiments.description: In rats with established opioid self-administration, give a single ibogaine dose and then sample brain, plasma and adipose ibogaine and noribogaine at intervals spanning the aftereffect, pairing every pharmacokinetic sample with a behavioural session in the same animals. Add two dissociating arms: a lipectomised or lean-versus-obese comparison that alters depot capacity without altering the administered dose, and a dosing regimen matched to reproduce the noribogaine concentration time-course without the parent compound.

experiment_type.preferred_term: paired pharmacokinetic and behavioural time-course experiment

perturbations.target: pathophysiology#Compulsive Opioid Seeking and Loss of Control
perturbations.description: The standard single-dose regimen whose aftereffect is the phenomenon in question.

perturbations.name: Depot capacity manipulation
perturbations.target: pathophysiology#Compulsive Opioid Seeking and Loss of Control
perturbations.description: Alteration of adipose depot capacity, holding administered dose constant, to change the predicted release profile without changing the pharmacodynamic exposure at dosing.

controls.name: Noribogaine-matched infusion without ibogaine
controls.description: Reproduces the metabolite exposure curve directly, separating sustained occupancy from anything the parent drug initiated.

readouts.name: Opioid intake at each time point paired with concurrent brain noribogaine
readouts.target: pathophysiology#Compulsive Opioid Seeking and Loss of Control
readouts.interpretation: The shape of the relation is the result: an aftereffect that tracks concurrent exposure is sustained occupancy, one that outlasts it is an induced change.

proposed_experiments.decision_criterion: If the aftereffect tracks concurrent brain noribogaine and scales with depot capacity, durability is pharmacokinetic and no induced-plasticity mechanism is required to explain it. If the aftereffect persists after exposure has fallen below target-engaging concentrations, a pharmacodynamic mechanism is required and the three competing hypotheses remain live.
supporting_outcome: Reduced opioid intake persisting after brain noribogaine falls below concentrations that engage any candidate target.
refuting_outcome: Aftereffect magnitude tracks concurrent exposure and scales with adipose depot capacity.

assertion.prompt: Does ibogaine change GDNF or BDNF in treated patients, given that the only human neurotrophin data in opioid dependence are cross-sectional baselines in which GDNF is unchanged and BDNF, not GDNF, tracks craving?
assertion.rationale: The neurotrophic hypothesis makes a human prediction it has never been asked to meet. In opiate-dependent patients, serum BDNF is elevated and correlates with heroin craving while serum GDNF is unchanged and uncorrelated. That is a negative for the GDNF-specific claim, but not a decisive one, because a cross-sectional baseline in maintenance patients does not test what the model predicts, which is a change in GDNF following a dose. Rodent ibogaine also raises BDNF broadly across nucleus accumbens, substantia nigra and prefrontal cortex, so even a positive human neurotrophin signal would need to distinguish a GDNF-specific response from a general one.

proposed_experiments.name: Serial neurotrophin response in ibogaine-treated patients
proposed_experiments.description: In a jurisdiction where ibogaine treatment is legal, collect serial plasma and where feasible cerebrospinal fluid GDNF and BDNF from patients before dosing and at intervals through twelve weeks, alongside withdrawal, craving and abstinence measures and CYP2D6 genotype. The comparison that matters is within-subject change from each patient's own baseline, which is what the existing cross-sectional study could not provide.

readouts.name: Within-subject change in GDNF from pre-dose baseline
readouts.interpretation: The model predicts a GDNF rise after dosing; an unchanged GDNF alongside a clinical response would place the burden on a non-neurotrophic mechanism.

readouts.name: Within-subject change in BDNF from pre-dose baseline
readouts.interpretation: Measured in parallel to test whether any neurotrophin response is GDNF-specific, as the model requires, or general.

proposed_experiments.decision_criterion: A GDNF rise that precedes and predicts the clinical response, and is larger than the concurrent BDNF change, supports the neurotrophic model in humans. An unchanged GDNF with a clinical response, or a BDNF-dominant response, argues that the human mechanism is not the one the rodent ethanol experiments identified.
supporting_outcome: GDNF rises from baseline after dosing and the rise predicts abstinence.
refuting_outcome: GDNF is unchanged after dosing in patients who nonetheless respond.

selected_evidence.snippet: Both doses elicited a large increase in the expression of BDNF transcripts in the NAcc, SN and PFC

assertion.prompt: Which of the three candidate mechanisms for ibogaine's anti-opioid effect is actually necessary for it, given that no study has ever infused ibogaine itself into a candidate site, or blocked a candidate receptor, while measuring opioid self-administration?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#VTA Disinhibition and Mesolimbic Dopamine Release
pathophysiology#Compulsive Opioid Seeking and Loss of Control
assertion.rationale: Three mechanisms compete to explain the same phenotype, and each rests on a different molecule or a different reinforcer. The GDNF route has a sufficiency-and-necessity pair, but for ethanol. The habenular route has a site dissociation, but for the congener 18-MC, which does not share ibogaine's neurotrophic actions. The kappa route has sufficiency from engineered analogues, not necessity for the parent drug. Ibogaine itself has never been microinjected into any site with an opioid reinforcer, and the only reported loss-of-function test against ibogaine is a partial reversal by a kappa antagonist combined with an NMDA agonist, reported once by the originating laboratory without isolating either action. Because all three routes converge on the same behavioural endpoint, demonstrating sufficiency for any one of them cannot establish that ibogaine works through it.

proposed_experiments.name: Intracerebral ibogaine site dissociation against opioid self-administration
proposed_experiments.description: Run the He 2005 and Glick 2006 designs on the parent drug rather than on a surrogate. Rats acquiring intravenous heroin or fentanyl self-administration receive ibogaine (or noribogaine) microinjected into the ventral tegmental area, the medial habenula, or the interpeduncular nucleus, with a sucrose or food arm run in parallel to test reinforcer selectivity. Measure intake acutely and at 24 hours and one week to separate the acute effect from the aftereffect, since the aftereffect is the property all three hypotheses were built to explain.

attaches_to: pathophysiology#Heparin-Independent Platelet Activation in Autoimmune HIT
assertion.prompt: How common is autoimmune HIT, and how many cases of delayed-onset, persisting, or spontaneous disease are being missed because the confirmatory test is not performed?
assertion.rationale: The autoimmune variant is defined by a laboratory property - platelet activation without heparin - that most HIT laboratories do not test for. That makes its true frequency unknowable from current practice, and creates a specific ascertainment trap: the patients most likely to be missed are those whose disease begins or persists after heparin has been stopped, which is exactly the group in whom the diagnosis is least likely to be entertained. The under-recognition is therefore not random with respect to severity, and any incidence figure for aHIT drawn from routine practice is a lower bound of unknown tightness.

selected_evidence.snippet: Intracranial bleeding and brain infarction caused her death.

attaches_to: pathophysiology#Heparin-Independent Platelet Activation in Autoimmune HIT
assertion.prompt: Are APTT-adjusted direct thrombin inhibitors the right treatment for autoimmune HIT, given that the same mechanism makes them both harder to dose and potentially counterproductive in that subset?
assertion.rationale: Two curated treatments in this entry pull against each other in the autoimmune subset, and the tension is mechanistic rather than merely practical. Direct thrombin inhibitors are the standard answer to HIT because thrombin generation is the effector node. But in aHIT two problems arise from the same biology. First, aHIT frequently comes with overt DIC, and DIC prolongs the APTT; because argatroban and bivalirudin are dosed to APTT, the prolongation causes systematic underdosing or interruption of the very drug the patient needs. Second, thrombin activates protein C, so inhibiting thrombin also suppresses the endogenous anticoagulant arm - the same protein C axis whose depletion causes venous limb gangrene when warfarin is given. The consequence is that the strongest evidence base in HIT (argatroban, from a prospective study against historical controls) was not generated in the subset where it is most likely to fail, and it is not settled what should replace it. IVIG addresses the receptor rather than thrombin, but it can fail too.

selected_evidence.snippet: or because DTI inhibits thrombin-induced protein C activation

attaches_to: pathophysiology#FcgammaRIIA-Mediated Platelet Activation by Immune Complexes
assertion.prompt: What distinguishes an anti-PF4/heparin IgG antibody that activates platelets from one that binds the same antigen and does nothing?
assertion.rationale: This is the gap that makes HIT hard to diagnose, and it sits precisely between two curated nodes. Antibodies against PF4-heparin complexes are common after heparin exposure; disease is not. The immunoassay detects binding and is therefore poorly specific, while the functional assay detects activation and is the reference standard but is technically demanding and not widely available. Restricting the immunoassay to IgG helps, which is consistent with FcgammaRIIA being the effector receptor, but it does not close the gap - most IgG-positive patients still do not have the disease. What is missing is a molecular account of the pathogenic property itself: which epitopes, what avidity or stoichiometry, what degree of complex clustering is required to cross-link FcgammaRIIA productively. Without it, no binding assay can be made specific, and the field is left with a reference standard that most laboratories cannot run.

proposed_experiments.name: Structural and functional dissection of platelet-activating versus non-activating anti-PF4 antibodies
proposed_experiments.description: Isolate paired activating and non-activating monoclonal antibodies from patients with and without clinical HIT, map their epitopes on the PF4-polyanion complex, and relate epitope location, avidity, and complex stoichiometry to FcgammaRIIA cross-linking efficiency in a functional platelet activation readout.

readouts.name: Platelet activation by epitope-defined monoclonal anti-PF4 antibodies
readouts.target: pathophysiology#FcgammaRIIA-Mediated Platelet Activation by Immune Complexes
readouts.interpretation: A structural correlate that separates activating from non-activating antibodies would allow a binding assay to be engineered for the pathogenic property rather than for the antigen.

attaches_to: pathophysiology#FcgammaRIIA-Mediated Platelet Activation by Immune Complexes
assertion.prompt: Why do only a minority of heparin-exposed patients mount a pathogenic anti-PF4/heparin response, and is any of that susceptibility inherited?
assertion.rationale: This entry carries no `genetic:` section, and the omission is deliberate rather than an oversight. Candidate loci exist and are biologically plausible - FCGR2A, which encodes the very receptor the central effector node turns on, plus TDAG8, HLA-DR, and a replicated chromosome 5 signal from a genome-wide association study - but genetic studies have not consistently identified risk alleles for HIT, for antibody production, or for its thromboembolic complications. Curating any of these as a risk gene would assert more than the evidence supports; the honest curation is that the absence of a validated determinant is itself the finding. The obstacles are structural rather than merely a matter of sample size: true HIT is scarce, misclassification is easy because the immunoassay is poorly specific, and the environmental exposure varies in type, dose, and duration. The consequence is that no pre-exposure test can currently identify who will develop HIT, which is the practical liability that accompanies every heparin prescription. Note also that the animal model curated in this entry cannot address the question at all: it bypasses the immune arm by injecting a monoclonal antibody rather than raising one.

proposed_experiments.name: Adequately powered multiethnic genetic study with laboratory-confirmed HIT
proposed_experiments.description: Assemble a multiethnic cohort with functional-assay-confirmed HIT rather than immunoassay-positive suspicion, capture heparin type, dose, and duration per patient, and analyse serologic and thromboembolic outcomes separately, since the same allele need not govern antibody formation and thrombosis.

readouts.name: Replicated association between a host variant and functionally confirmed HIT
readouts.interpretation: A determinant that survives laboratory confirmation and replication would convert an unpredictable adverse drug reaction into a screenable one.

selected_evidence.snippet: Compelling evidence also suggests that the FCGR2A H131R polymorphism is associated with HIT-related thrombosis.

Second, thrombin activates protein C, so inhibiting thrombin also suppresses the endogenous anticoagulant arm - the same protein C axis whose depletion causes venous limb gangrene when warfarin is given. The consequence is that the strongest evidence base in HIT (argatroban, from a prospective study against historical controls) was not generated in the subset where it is most likely to fail, and it is not settled what should replace it. IVIG addresses the receptor rather than thrombin, but it can fail too.

attaches_to: pathophysiology#FcgammaRIIA-Mediated Platelet Activation by Immune Complexes
value.prompt: What distinguishes an anti-PF4/heparin IgG antibody that activates platelets from one that binds the same antigen and does nothing?
value.rationale: This is the gap that makes HIT hard to diagnose, and it sits precisely between two curated nodes. Antibodies against PF4-heparin complexes are common after heparin exposure; disease is not. The immunoassay detects binding and is therefore poorly specific, while the functional assay detects activation and is the reference standard but is technically demanding and not widely available. Restricting the immunoassay to IgG helps, which is consistent with FcgammaRIIA being the effector receptor, but it does not close the gap - most IgG-positive patients still do not have the disease. What is missing is a molecular account of the pathogenic property itself: which epitopes, what avidity or stoichiometry, what degree of complex clustering is required to cross-link FcgammaRIIA productively. Without it, no binding assay can be made specific, and the field is left with a reference standard that most laboratories cannot run.

attaches_to: pathophysiology#FcgammaRIIA-Mediated Platelet Activation by Immune Complexes
assertion.prompt: Why do only a minority of heparin-exposed patients mount a pathogenic anti-PF4/heparin response, and is any of that susceptibility inherited?
assertion.rationale: This entry carries no `genetic:` section, and the omission is deliberate rather than an oversight. Candidate loci exist and are biologically plausible - FCGR2A, which encodes the very receptor the central effector node turns on, plus TDAG8, HLA-DR, and a replicated chromosome 5 signal from a genome-wide association study - but genetic studies have not consistently identified risk alleles for HIT, for antibody production, or for its thromboembolic complications. Curating any of these as a risk gene would assert more than the evidence supports; the honest curation is that the absence of a validated determinant is itself the finding. The obstacles are structural rather than merely a matter of sample size: true HIT is scarce, misclassification is easy because the immunoassay is poorly specific, and the environmental exposure varies in type, dose, and duration. The consequence is that no pre-exposure test can currently identify who will develop HIT, which is the practical liability that accompanies every heparin prescription. Note also that the animal model curated in this entry cannot address the question at all: it bypasses the immune arm by injecting a monoclonal antibody rather than raising one.

assertion.prompt: Can alpha-synuclein aggregates taken from human peripheral sympathetic ganglia actually seed and propagate pathology, as the mouse fibril-injection model of PAF assumes?
assertion.rationale: The animal model in this entry seeds pathology by injecting synthetic preformed fibrils into the ganglia of mice overexpressing mutant human alpha-synuclein, and the pathology then spreads along autonomic pathways into the central nervous system. That result is the main experimental support for the phenoconversion node. But when Lewy-body aggregates purified from the stellate ganglia of Parkinson disease patients were inoculated into mouse brain, they produced neither pathology nor degeneration, while aggregates from the same patients' substantia nigra did. So the seeding competence demonstrated in the model may be a property of synthetic fibrils in a transgenic host rather than of the human peripheral aggregate the model stands for. This is a mismatch rather than a missing experiment: evidence exists on both sides and points in opposite directions, and what is unresolved is whether the human peripheral aggregate propagates at all.

proposed_experiments.name: Seeding competence of PAF-derived ganglionic aggregates
proposed_experiments.description: Purify alpha-synuclein aggregates from sympathetic ganglia of autopsy-confirmed PAF cases, rather than from Parkinson disease cases or from synthetic fibrils, and test them both in seed amplification assays and by inoculation into the ganglia of wild-type and TgM83 mice. The published negative result used Parkinson disease stellate ganglia and inoculated the brain, so it leaves the PAF aggregate and the peripheral route untested.
supporting_outcome: Pathology propagating from the injected ganglion in a wild-type host would support peripheral-to-central spread as a mechanism of phenoconversion in PAF, independent of transgene overexpression.
refuting_outcome: A PAF-derived aggregate that seeds in vitro but propagates in no host would make the model's spread result an artefact of synthetic fibrils and would leave phenoconversion unexplained by propagation.

assertion.prompt: Does a stable, purely peripheral PAF exist, or would every case phenoconvert given long enough follow-up?
assertion.rationale: The entry records the conversion rate well - about 30 percent of patients, a pooled 5.09 per 100 person-years, with MSA clustering in the first years while Lewy body disorders arrive at a steadier rate. What it cannot say is what the other 70 percent are. If the Lewy body rate is genuinely constant, a cohort followed long enough would see most of them convert, and PAF would be a stage of a central synucleinopathy rather than a disease with an endpoint of its own. The meta-analysis reports that heterogeneity between studies was partly explained by follow-up duration, which is the signature of censoring rather than of a biologically distinct group that never converts. The alternative is that some patients carry a peripherally restricted lesion that never ascends, which is what the sympathetic-predominant body-first hypothesis would predict for a subset, and which the autopsy series behind that hypothesis observed in people who had not been diagnosed with anything. No cohort in this entry distinguishes the two readings, and they differ in what a prognosis should say to a patient diagnosed today.

proposed_experiments.name: Autopsy-anchored follow-up of long-standing non-converters
proposed_experiments.description: Follow patients who have carried a PAF diagnosis for more than ten years without motor or cognitive signs until death, with brain and peripheral autonomic autopsy, and compare their alpha-synuclein distribution with that of converters and with the incidental Lewy body cases staged as sympathetic-predominant. Clinical follow-up alone cannot settle this, because a patient who dies without motor signs may still carry central pathology; only the autopsy distinguishes a lesion that never ascended from one that ascended without becoming symptomatic.
supporting_outcome: Long-standing non-converters whose pathology at autopsy remains confined to peripheral sympathetic tissue would establish a peripherally restricted form, and would make PAF a disease with its own endpoint rather than a stage.
refuting_outcome: Central Lewy pathology in clinically pure long-standing cases would show that ascent is the rule and that non-conversion is a statement about symptoms rather than about distribution, leaving PAF a prodromal stage in every case.

selected_evidence.snippet: Within 4 years of follow-up, 25 of 74 subjects (34%) developed dementia with Lewy bodies (n = 13), Parkinson disease (n = 6), or multiple system atrophy (n = 6).

assertion.prompt: What genetic contribution does PAF have, given that it is consistently described as sporadic and has never been subject to an association study?
assertion.rationale: This entry has no genetic section, and that is a decision rather than an omission: the reviews describe PAF as sporadic, and SNCA appears on pathophysiology nodes as the gene of the aggregating protein rather than as a cause. But sporadic is a statement about family history, not about susceptibility, and the related synucleinopathies have common-variant architecture that PAF has not been tested for. A PubMed search for a genome-wide association study of pure autonomic failure returns no records (searched 2026-10-27, pure autonomic failure AND genome-wide association, 0 records; the eleven hits for a broader genetic-association query are reviews, other diseases, or unrelated). The genetic evidence that does touch the PAF phenotype comes from rare monogenic families rather than from PAF cohorts: SNCA triplication produces the cardiac noradrenergic lesion, and E46K carriers include people whose clinical diagnosis is PAF. So whether PAF carries risk alleles, whether GBA or SNCA variants shift which central disease a patient converts to, and whether the non-Lewy preganglionic form has a different architecture are all untested rather than answered. This is a resource gap, not a conceptual one, and it is recorded so the absence is not read as a negative result.

proposed_experiments.name: Genotyping of PAF cohorts against synucleinopathy risk architecture
proposed_experiments.description: Genotype the existing multicentre PAF cohorts, which are already assembled for phenoconversion follow-up, for the common variants established in Parkinson disease and dementia with Lewy bodies and for GBA and SNCA, and test both for association with the PAF diagnosis and for association with the conversion target within the cohort. PAF is too rare for a well-powered genome-wide study of its own, so the tractable question is whether known synucleinopathy risk loci are enriched and whether they stratify conversion, which the follow-up data already collected would answer.
supporting_outcome: Enrichment of established synucleinopathy risk alleles in PAF would place the peripheral aggregation lesion inside the same susceptibility architecture as the central Lewy body diseases, and a genotype that predicted the conversion target would give the two subtype hypotheses a genetic correlate.
refuting_outcome: No enrichment at loci well established in Parkinson disease and dementia with Lewy bodies would argue the peripheral form has a distinct susceptibility architecture, and would weaken reading PAF as the peripheral presentation of the same disease process.

selected_evidence.snippet: We studied 7 E46K-SNCA carriers (3 dementia with Lewy bodies, 2 pure autonomic failure, 1 PD and 1 asymptomatic)

assertion.prompt: Can treatment given during the peripheral phase of PAF prevent phenoconversion, and is the peripheral lesion still the right target by the time PAF is diagnosed?
assertion.rationale: Every treatment in this entry is symptomatic, and the entry records that nothing slows progression or phenoconversion. The field's stated plan is to use PAF as a prodromal population and biomarkers to select who enters a disease-modification trial. Two things already in this entry argue that the target may be wrong. By the time PAF is diagnosed the postganglionic noradrenergic lesion is severe - plasma norepinephrine is very low and cardiac tracer uptake largely gone - so a therapy meant to protect peripheral neurons arrives after most of them are affected, which is the same question the functional-versus-structural gap asks. And a therapy aimed instead at preventing ascent targets propagation, the step this entry's HUMAN_MODEL_MISMATCH discussion records as unproven in PAF, since aggregates from human peripheral tissue failed to seed and only synthetic fibrils spread in the transgenic host. So the prodromal window here is defined clinically, by the absence of motor and cognitive signs, and not by the presence of neurons left to save or of a propagation step shown to occur. Which of the two a trial should target is open, and the choice decides what the endpoint and the enrolment window should be.

proposed_experiments.name: Biomarker-stratified prevention trial with phenoconversion as the endpoint
proposed_experiments.description: Enrol patients with PAF stratified by the markers this entry already records as predicting the conversion target - supine norepinephrine, cardiac 18F-dopamine pattern, CSF neurofilament light chain and seed amplification - and randomise to an alpha-synuclein-directed agent or placebo with phenoconversion as the primary endpoint. Stratification is not a refinement here but the design: the entry's two subtype hypotheses predict different conversion targets on different timescales, so an unstratified trial pools patients whose event rates and mechanisms differ.
supporting_outcome: A reduction in phenoconversion under an alpha-synuclein-directed agent would establish propagation as both real and interruptible in PAF, which no model result currently shows for human peripheral aggregates.
refuting_outcome: No effect on phenoconversion despite engagement of the target would favour central disease arising independently of peripheral spread, and would leave the entry's phenoconversion node without its proposed mechanism.

selected_evidence.snippet: providing an invaluable opportunity for early diagnosis and intervention

assertion.prompt: What starts alpha-synuclein aggregating in peripheral autonomic neurons in PAF, and does the catecholaldehyde DOPAL accumulate in those neurons before the aggregates appear?
assertion.rationale: The entry's canonical chain begins at aggregation, and the aggregation node says the initiating trigger is unknown. The catecholaldehyde node upstream of it rests on cell-free chemistry, postmortem tissue from other Lewy body diseases and a computational model; nothing has measured DOPAL, aldehyde dehydrogenase activity or the DOPAC:DOPAL ratio in sympathetic tissue from patients with PAF. The gap matters for more than completeness, because the two interventions the hypothesis implies - inhibiting monoamine oxidase to make less DOPAL, and antioxidant treatment to stop its oxidation - are both available, and PAF is the one Lewy body disease where the affected neurons are accessible by skin and vein biopsy. The author of the hypothesis lists the PAF form of the question explicitly as unanswered.

proposed_experiments.name: Catecholaldehyde measurement in biopsied sympathetic tissue from PAF patients
proposed_experiments.description: Quantify DOPAL, DOPAC, the DOPAC:DOPAL ratio and aldehyde dehydrogenase activity in forearm vein and skin biopsies from patients with PAF, from patients with the non-Lewy preganglionic form, and from controls, in the same samples used to assay tyrosine hydroxylase and VMAT2. The vein-biopsy protocol that established the vesicular storage defect in PAF already yields the tissue; what has not been measured is the aldehyde.
supporting_outcome: A raised DOPAL level or a lowered DOPAC:DOPAL ratio in PAF sympathetic tissue, tracking the vesicular storage defect in the same samples, would support the autotoxic step acting in this disease rather than only in vitro.
refuting_outcome: Normal DOPAL handling in sympathetic tissue carrying heavy alpha-synuclein deposits would refute the catecholaldehyde step in PAF and leave aggregation as the entry point of the chain.

proposed_experiments.name: Longitudinal catecholaldehyde and vesicular-storage markers across phenoconversion
proposed_experiments.description: Follow a PAF cohort already undergoing serial cardiac 18F-dopamine PET and CSF seed amplification, adding catecholaldehyde-pathway markers at each visit, to test whether the aldehyde burden moves before or after the storage defect and the seeding signal. The computational model of this mechanism predicts a specific three-phase order, which makes it falsifiable by serial measurement.
supporting_outcome: Aldehyde-pathway change preceding measurable loss of vesicular sequestration, in the order the model predicts, would support the loop running in the direction the hypothesis claims.
refuting_outcome: Aldehyde change appearing only after denervation is established would make it a consequence of the lesion rather than its cause.

proposed_experiments.name: Reconstruction of the catecholaldehyde loop in human iPSC-derived sympathetic neurons
proposed_experiments.description: Impose the aldehyde burden on the cell type this entry is about. Human pluripotent stem cells are differentiated to postganglionic sympathetic neurons, aldehyde dehydrogenase is inhibited to raise DOPAL without adding it from outside, and alpha-synuclein oligomer load, vesicular norepinephrine storage and stimulated norepinephrine release are measured in the same cultures. The existing cell models of the catecholaldehyde step use a neuroblastoma line, mouse cortical neurons or a glial line, and supply DOPAL in the medium, so neither the affected cell type nor the endogenous route to the aldehyde has been tested; these neurons secrete norepinephrine on activation, which is the quantity PAF loses. A patient-derived line is deliberately not the design here. PAF is sporadic with no causal gene, so an unselected patient line carries no lesion to express, which is why the protocol's established use is a Mendelian autonomic disease rather than this one.

model_systems.name: Human iPSC-derived postganglionic sympathetic neurons
model_systems.description: Sympathetic neurons differentiated from human pluripotent stem cells by way of neural crest, maintained as monocultures or co-cultured with iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes. They carry tyrosine hydroxylase, fire action potentials, secrete norepinephrine on stimulation, and in co-culture drive the beating rate of the myocytes they innervate, so the noradrenergic functions this entry's nodes describe are all directly measurable.
model_systems.culture_system: Feeder-free monolayer differentiation through neural crest, with an optional neurocardiac co-culture arm against iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes

modeled_mechanisms.description: Supplies the cell type the node names, so the aldehyde burden, the oligomer load and the storage defect can be measured in one system and in the right neuron rather than inferred across three unrelated ones.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: These neurons are weeks old and were never exposed to whatever initiates the disease, so a loop demonstrated in them shows the mechanism can run in a human sympathetic neuron, not that it is what runs in a patient.

divergences.description: PAF has no causal lesion to encode, so the aldehyde burden has to be imposed pharmacologically by inhibiting aldehyde dehydrogenase. The model therefore tests whether the loop can run, and cannot establish that it starts this way in the disease.
A culture runs for weeks against a disease that takes decades and whose own progression node is measured in years of serial imaging, so an acute aldehyde challenge stands in for chronic accumulation.
Preganglionic input, the baroreflex arc and the vasculature are outside the model. Immaterial to this experiment, whose claims are confined to events inside the postganglionic neuron.

readouts.name: Intraneuronal DOPAL and DOPAC to DOPAL ratio after aldehyde dehydrogenase inhibition
readouts.interpretation: Confirms the intended perturbation was achieved from the cell's own dopamine rather than supplied from outside, which is what the existing cell models cannot show.

readouts.name: Alpha-synuclein oligomer load in sympathetic neurons
readouts.interpretation: Tests whether an endogenously generated aldehyde burden is sufficient to aggregate alpha-synuclein in the cell type that aggregates it in patients.

readouts.name: Vesicular norepinephrine content and stimulated release
readouts.target: pathophysiology#Noradrenergic Vesicular Storage and Synthesis Defect
readouts.interpretation: The return arm of the loop, measured as the function PAF loses rather than as dopamine leak from a vesicle preparation.

proposed_experiments.decision_criterion: The three readouts are read in order. An aldehyde rise followed by oligomer accumulation followed by loss of vesicular storage establishes that the loop can run in a human sympathetic neuron. An aldehyde rise with no oligomer accumulation places the burden of the hypothesis back on the cell-free chemistry.
supporting_outcome: Oligomer accumulation and loss of vesicular norepinephrine storage following an endogenously generated aldehyde burden, in human sympathetic neurons, would move the catecholaldehyde step off cell-free chemistry and out of the wrong cell types for the first time.
refuting_outcome: A raised aldehyde burden that leaves alpha-synuclein unaggregated and storage intact in the cell type the hypothesis is about would weigh against the step, and would suggest the oligomerisation seen in neuroblastoma and glial lines depends on conditions those systems impose.

selected_evidence.snippet: The extent to which DOPAL toxicity is mediated by interactions with αS, and vice versa, is poorly understood.

By the time PAF is diagnosed the postganglionic noradrenergic lesion is severe - plasma norepinephrine is very low and cardiac tracer uptake largely gone - so a therapy meant to protect peripheral neurons arrives after most of them are affected, which is the same question the functional-versus-structural gap asks. And a therapy aimed instead at preventing ascent targets propagation, the step this entry's HUMAN_MODEL_MISMATCH discussion records as unproven in PAF, since aggregates from human peripheral tissue failed to seed and only synthetic fibrils spread in the transgenic host. So the prodromal window here is defined clinically, by the absence of motor and cognitive signs, and not by the presence of neurons left to save or of a propagation step shown to occur. Which of the two a trial should target is open, and the choice decides what the endpoint and the enrolment window should be.

proposed_experiments.name: Biomarker-stratified prevention trial with phenoconversion as the endpoint
proposed_experiments.description: Enrol patients with PAF stratified by the markers this entry already records as predicting the conversion target - supine norepinephrine, cardiac 18F-dopamine pattern, CSF neurofilament light chain and seed amplification - and randomise to an alpha-synuclein-directed agent or placebo with phenoconversion as the primary endpoint. Stratification is not a refinement here but the design: the entry's two subtype hypotheses predict different conversion targets on different timescales, so an unstratified trial pools patients whose event rates and mechanisms differ.
supporting_outcome: A reduction in phenoconversion under an alpha-synuclein-directed agent would establish propagation as both real and interruptible in PAF, which no model result currently shows for human peripheral aggregates.
refuting_outcome: No effect on phenoconversion despite engagement of the target would favour central disease arising independently of peripheral spread, and would leave the entry's phenoconversion node without its proposed mechanism.

selected_evidence.snippet: The discovery of specific paths mediating the sick-but-not-dead phenomenon offers novel targets for multi-pronged therapeutic approaches.

assertion.prompt: What are the ADCA-DN-specific age at onset, survival, and rate of cognitive decline, as opposed to the figures derived from HSAN1E and mixed DNMT1-complex cohorts?
assertion.rationale: The most frequently quoted DNMT1 natural-history numbers (mean onset 37.7 years, average survival 53.6 years, significant cognitive deficit in 89 percent by age 45) come from a cohort of nine HSAN1E kinships comprising 45 affected subjects. In the source abstract these figures are attributed explicitly to HSAN1E, not to ADCA-DN. Because HSAN1E and ADCA-DN are discrete clinical entities with different variant positions within the same domain, these values are deliberately not recorded as ADCA-DN prevalence, progression, or prognosis in this entry. No registry-scale ADCA-DN natural history cohort exists, and no variant-specific penetrance estimate is available.

proposed_experiments.name: International DNMT1 registry stratified by targeting-sequence variant position
proposed_experiments.description: Assemble an international registry of genetically confirmed DNMT1 patients with prospective standardized assessment of ataxia scales, audiometry, polysomnography, neuropsychology, and survival, analyzed with strata defined by variant position within the targeting-sequence domain (C-terminal/exon 21 versus middle and N-terminal/exon 20) rather than by clinical label alone.
proposed_experiments.decision_criterion: Stratified onset, survival, and cognitive-decline curves that differ significantly between variant-position strata would establish ADCA-DN-specific natural history and confirm that pooled DNMT1 figures are not transferable.

assertion.prompt: Do the existing DNMT1 RFTS knock-in mice model ADCA-DN, given that they carry HSAN1E-equivalent alleles and do not develop narcolepsy, deafness, or cerebellar ataxia?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#Relief of RFTS Autoinhibition and DNMT1 Destabilization
assertion.rationale: The only published knock-in mice carry mouse equivalents of the human HSAN1E variants Y495C and D490E-P491Y, which lie in the middle or N-terminal part of the targeting-sequence domain, not the C-terminal exon-21 region that defines ADCA-DN. Since intradomain variant position is the principal determinant separating the two human phenotypes, a model built on HSAN1E alleles cannot be assumed to capture the ADCA-DN phenotype. The heterozygous mice show reduced DNMT1 protein and impaired learning and memory, but the three defining ADCA-DN features (narcolepsy, sensorineural deafness, cerebellar ataxia) have not been demonstrated. Mechanistic conclusions from these mice about RFTS destabilization and cleavage are recorded as PARTIAL support for that reason. A 2025 follow-up using RFTS-mutant mice identified aberrant DNMT1-dependent RNA m5C methylation, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial dysfunction. Its published abstract does not name the mouse RFTS allele or establish translation to classical exon-21 ADCA-DN, so that branch is likewise recorded as provisional, PARTIAL support rather than an established ADCA-DN mechanism.

proposed_experiments.name: Exon-21-allele knock-in mouse with longitudinal sleep, auditory, and cerebellar phenotyping
proposed_experiments.description: Generate heterozygous knock-in mice carrying the mouse equivalent of human DNMT1 p.Ala570Val or p.Val606Phe and phenotype them longitudinally with EEG/EMG sleep architecture and cataplexy scoring, hypothalamic hypocretin neuron counts, auditory brainstem responses and distortion-product otoacoustic emissions, rotarod and gait analysis with cerebellar histology, DNA methylome and RNA m5C profiling resolved by cell type, and mitochondrial functional assays. Run the existing HSAN1E-allele lines side by side as comparators.
proposed_experiments.decision_criterion: Emergence of sleep-onset REM intrusion, cataplexy-like attacks, elevated auditory brainstem response thresholds, and progressive cerebellar degeneration in the exon-21 line but not the HSAN1E lines would establish phenotype dependence on allele position and give the field a genuine ADCA-DN model.

selected_evidence.snippet: We generated Dnmt1-M1 and Dnmt1-M2 knock-in mouse models that are equivalent to Y495C and D490E-P491Y mutation in patients with HSAN1E, respectively.

assertion.prompt: Is there any tractable disease-modifying strategy for ADCA-DN, given that the mechanism combines impaired maintenance methylation with potentially toxic mutant-protein species?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#Mutant DNMT1 Mislocalization and Aggresome Formation
assertion.rationale: No approved or investigational disease-modifying drug, gene therapy, RNA therapy, or epigenome-editing treatment exists for ADCA-DN, and no disease-specific interventional clinical trial has been registered. The mechanism is not a clean loss of function, so simple gene supplementation is unlikely to be sufficient and broad DNMT inhibition would be expected to be harmful. Allele-selective silencing of the mutant transcript, or pharmacological correction of mutant-protein mislocalization and aggresome formation, are the mechanistically plausible directions but neither has been attempted.

proposed_experiments.name: Allele-selective mutant DNMT1 knockdown in patient-derived induced neurons
proposed_experiments.description: In induced neurons from ADCA-DN patients carrying p.Ala570Val, p.Gly605Ala, or p.Val606Phe, apply allele-selective antisense oligonucleotides or base editing to reduce the mutant transcript while preserving the wild-type allele, then measure DNMT1 subcellular localization, aggresome burden, autophagic flux, and reversal of the patient methylome and transcriptome signature.
proposed_experiments.decision_criterion: Normalization of DNMT1 localization and of the patient methylome and transcriptome signature without loss of total maintenance methylation would support allele-selective knockdown as a therapeutic direction.

selected_evidence.snippet: Our results suggest mutations in DNMT1 result in imbalanced protein homeostasis through aggresome-induced autophagy.

assertion.prompt: Does ADCA-DN produce net hypermethylation of normally unmethylated regions, bidirectional change that depends on locus and cell type, or both depending on the tissue examined?
assertion.rationale: A genome-wide array on DNA from a six-affected ADCA-DN family found a shift out of the lowest and upper-intermediate methylation bins into intermediate and near-complete methylation, with 82 regionally hypermethylated loci, consistent with increased methylation of normally unmethylated promoters and CpG islands. In contrast, patient fibroblasts, iPSCs, and induced neurons showed changes whose direction depended on cell type, including ZFP57 promoter hypomethylation with increased ZFP57 expression. Neither result supports the older global-hypomethylation model, but they are not obviously reconcilable with each other, and the tissue examined differs (peripheral blood-derived DNA versus derived neural cells). Resolving this determines whether any methylation episignature could serve as a diagnostic or pharmacodynamic biomarker.

proposed_experiments.name: Matched multi-tissue methylome comparison in the same ADCA-DN carriers
proposed_experiments.description: Profile whole-genome bisulfite methylomes from peripheral blood, skin fibroblasts, and iPSC-derived neurons from the same set of ADCA-DN carriers and matched controls, using one analysis pipeline, and test whether the direction of change at shared loci is concordant across tissues or genuinely dependent on tissue.
proposed_experiments.decision_criterion: Concordant direction across tissues would indicate that the earlier discrepancy was methodological; discordant direction at shared loci would confirm a genuine dependence on cell type and rule out a single blood-based episignature.

selected_evidence.snippet: Furthermore, ZFP57, which is required to maintain gene imprinting through DNA methylation during early development, was hypomethylated in promoters and exhibited upregulated expression in patients with ADCA-DN in both iPSC and iNs.

assertion.prompt: Which cell populations actually degenerate in the ADCA-DN cerebellum and auditory system, and would that support conformance to the cerebellar_purkinje_degeneration and sensorineural_hair_cell_loss modules?
assertion.rationale: Conformance to both modules was evaluated and declined. The cerebellar_purkinje_degeneration module turns on Purkinje neuron degeneration as its central effector, but the only ADCA-DN cerebellar data are MRI atrophy and a raised MR spectroscopy myo-inositol signal, which reflects glial density rather than Purkinje loss; no autopsy series exists. The sensorineural_hair_cell_loss module turns on hair cell mechanotransduction failure and death, whereas the ADCA-DN deafness is described as sensory neuronal and is accompanied by attenuated brainstem auditory evoked potentials, which points to auditory-neural or retrocochlear rather than hair cell pathology. Declaring conformance in either case would assert an effector cell type that has not been demonstrated. Both decisions should be revisited if neuropathological or temporal-bone data appear.

proposed_experiments.name: Cerebellar and temporal-bone neuropathology in ADCA-DN donors
proposed_experiments.description: In ADCA-DN brain and temporal-bone donations, perform calbindin and parvalbumin immunohistochemistry with stereological Purkinje cell counts and Bergmann glia assessment in the cerebellar cortex, and cytocochleogram analysis of inner and outer hair cells together with spiral ganglion neuron counts in the temporal bone.
proposed_experiments.decision_criterion: Significant Purkinje cell loss relative to age-matched controls would justify conformance to cerebellar_purkinje_degeneration; a hair-cell-loss cytocochleogram pattern would justify conformance to sensorineural_hair_cell_loss, whereas isolated spiral ganglion or auditory nerve loss would confirm the retrocochlear interpretation and the decision to decline.
